summary: Myrtle branches are gathered for booths at Jerusalem. Isaiah names the myrtle among the trees Yahweh will plant in the wilderness, and Zechariah sees a rider standing among myrtles.

senses.definition: A shrub or small tree whose leafy branches could be cut for shelter.

evidence.note: The proclamation lists myrtle branches alongside olive and palm branches as material for making booths.
Yahweh promises to put myrtle alongside cedar and acacia in the wilderness.
The myrtle comes up where the nettle grew, as the cypress comes up in place of the thorn.
The rider on the red horse stands among a group of myrtles in a hollow.

evidence.locator: E00139, referring to E00138 and Targum Zechariah 1:8
Arabic هدس, plant noun and proposed borrowing from Hebrew

note: The same plant name occurs on both sides of the Red Sea. Anderson and Moser group the Hebrew, Aramaic and Geʽez forms under a common ancestor. The Arabic dictionary entry instead proposes borrowing from Hebrew and transmission through Arabic into Ethiopian languages. The forms establish a shared plant name more securely than its route of transmission.
